newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican police seize alleged leader of EPR rebels.
newsitem.headline: Mexican police seize alleged leader of EPR rebels.

text.p: Mexican police on Monday arrested a well-known peasant activist on charges he was a figurehead of the rebel Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR) that launched a series of violent attacks last year.

In a statement, the Interior Ministry said Mexico City police seized Benigno Guzman Martinez near his home in the capital then sent him to Chilpancingo, capital of southern Guerrero state, where the EPR first appeared last year.

"The name of Mr. Guzman Martinez was mentioned by detained persons facing trial on a number of counts, in reference to his participation as the main organiser of the first appearance of the EPR in the village of Aguas Blancas, Guerrero, on June 28, 1996," the ministry said.

The statement did not give information about Guzman's past. However, an attorney general's office spokesman in Chilpancingo said he was the leader of the OCSS, a local peasant group that officials have long linked to the EPR.

Some 17 OCSS members were slain by state police in the village of Aguas Blancas in 1995, an incident that may have helped create the EPR, which made its debut appearance, symbolically, exactly one year later at a rally to mark the massacre.
After the EPR's appearance, Guzman went underground, though his residence in Mexico City was an open secret.
His estranged brother, Bartolo, also a peasant leader who backed the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party, was shot and killed by masked gunmen near Aguas Blancas in December.

Since it emerged in June, the EPR has launched several attacks against military and police targets, the most bloody being a coordinated strike across several states in August in which at least 20 people died.
Conflict has died down recently, however, and the rebels have limited their actions to propaganda rallies and the issuing of communiques.
The Interior Ministry said Guzman would be prosecuted in Chilpancingo over his alleged links to the EPR.
